lead.headline: Alberta votes 76% to stay in Canada, rejecting a separation path
lead.dek: Smith promises no second vote this mandate; separatists say they will test her hold on the UCP
body: Albertans voted by a wide margin Monday to remain in Canada, with early returns showing about 76% rejecting a path toward a binding separation referendum, Global News and CTV News reported as Elections Alberta counted ballots overnight in the nonbinding vote called by Premier Danielle Smith's government.

CTV News projected 76.4% for remaining and 23.6% for beginning the legal process toward a separation vote, with the remain side passing 1 million votes shortly before 1 a.m. MT. More than 1.35 million ballots were cast in advance polls and by mail, Global News reported, against about 810,000 cast that way in the 2023 provincial election.

Smith, who said she voted to remain, had promised that 50% plus one would carry the day and that there would be no follow-up referendum in this mandate; she addresses the province Tuesday at 6:45 p.m. MT. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Albertans "chose unity." Results on nine other questions, on immigration and the Constitution, are expected Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Trump says someone else should negotiate for Ukraine
briefs.summary: Trump said Monday "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine" and that Zelenskyy "doesn't want to stop it." Zelenskyy meets U.S. negotiators this week.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court turns away 9/11 plea deal appeal
briefs.summary: The court let stand a ruling that the Pentagon could withdraw 2024 plea deals for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and two co-defendants. A military trial is set for June 2028.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq rises 1.1% as chip stocks rebound from sell-off
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq closed at 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 added 0.41% to 7,690.73 Monday; the Dow slipped 0.07%. Micron rose 2.97% after last week's AI-driven slide.

briefs.headline: Nor'easter brings coastal flooding to the Carolina coast
briefs.summary: Forecasters said an offshore nor'easter could push 1 to 4 feet of water into coastal North Carolina and up to a foot from Virginia to New Jersey, with gusts to 40 mph, through midweek.

briefs.headline: Houthi missiles kill at least 53 soldiers at Yemen camp
briefs.summary: Yemeni military officials gave the toll for Monday's strike on a camp in Shabwa province; the provincial government said 200 recruits were wounded.

briefs.headline: Drone attacks across Sudan kill more than 160 since Friday
briefs.summary: Medics and rights groups gave the toll. Residents and medical workers said a Sunday strike on a transport hub in West Kordofan killed 80.

briefs.headline: France imposes overnight curfews in Paris, Lyon and Nice
briefs.summary: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the localized curfews kept the peace overnight and may return Tuesday; early estimates put 3,000 businesses hit.

briefs.headline: Australian MP Helen Haines loses leg after car attack
briefs.summary: ABC and the Sydney Morning Herald reported the amputation. Albanese said she remains critical after surgery; a 43-year-old driver is in custody.

briefs.headline: Boone jury convicts grandmother in teen's starvation death
briefs.summary: A Boone County jury found Donna Stone guilty Monday of murder by child neglect and neglect causing death in Kyneddi Miller's 2024 death; it returns today to weigh mercy.

briefs.headline: GOP registration edge tops 200,000 as early voting nears
briefs.summary: Republicans hold 527,532 registrations to Democrats' 326,697, a 200,835 edge as of Oct. 13, the Secretary of State's report shows. Early voting runs Oct. 21-31.

briefs.headline: WVDNR stocks nearly 40 waters with 40,000 pounds of trout
briefs.summary: The DNR's fall stocking runs the weeks of Oct. 19 and Oct. 26, one stocking per water each week; locations are in the 2026 fishing regulations summary.

briefs.headline: Glenville oilman and donor Ike Morris dies
briefs.summary: Morris founded Waco Oil & Gas in 1975 and funded Glenville State's arena and stadium; his daughter announced his death Monday. Morrisey and Justice issued tributes.

regional.item: Cabell commissioners publicly tested about eight pieces of election tabulation equipment Monday ahead of early voting Oct. 21.
Charleston council voted Monday to seek a $2.4M National Park Service grant toward $4.6M of work on the Cato Park and Kanawha City pools.
Wood County's board set attendance lines for the new Lincoln and Vienna elementaries opening in 2027-28; parent meetings start tonight.
Summers County ARH's main entrance and front lot in Hinton closed Monday for two to four weeks of paving for a new emergency department.

away.item: Police charged a Shaftsbury man, 67, with manslaughter in a May 31 Dorset driveway death; he turned himself in Oct. 15, the Banner said.

hotspots.item: A Curtin educator received West Virginia Adult Education's Rising Strong Award for rebuilding the adult-ed program at Central Regional Jail, the Echo said Oct. 13.
North Topsail Beach set a Nov. 4 public hearing on adding parking definitions and penalties to its public-safety code, the town posted Monday.

briefs.headline: Kirk, Alan win last two Fraser-Fort George rural seats
briefs.summary: Jerrilyn Kirk kept Area G with about 90% and Dannielle Alan won Area H, completing the regional district board; Ken Schinkel took the six-candidate Area D race.

briefs.headline: Thompson keeps Robson Valley school trustee seat
briefs.summary: Bob Thompson took 248 votes to Lianne Abbott's 196 in the last Prince George school board result to come in; the district's results page shows 56,052 ballots cast.

briefs.headline: Lytton mayoral race heads to judicial recount after 45-45 tie
briefs.summary: Incumbent Denise O'Connor and challenger Jennifer Thoss each took 45 votes in results the village posted Monday. If the recount holds, the bylaw calls for drawing lots.

briefs.headline: B.C. advance turnout runs 8% below 2024 after three days
briefs.summary: About 440,000 ballots were cast Friday through Sunday, about 12% of registered voters, against roughly 480,000 in 2024, The Canadian Press reported; advance polls close Wednesday at 8 p.m.

briefs.headline: Canada's inflation rate rises to 3.1% in September
briefs.summary: Statistics Canada said gasoline rose 27.8% from a year earlier while the CPI excluding gasoline slowed to 2.2% and grocery prices to 1.7%, the smallest rise since May 2024.

briefs.headline: JAXA launches Phobos sample mission on H3 rocket
briefs.summary: The MMX spacecraft lifted off from Tanegashima at 3:41 p.m. ET Monday and separated from the H3's upper stage 71 minutes later in its planned orbit, JAXA said. It is to land on Phobos and bring samples home.

briefs.headline: Gulf deep-sea life fell 60% after Deepwater Horizon
briefs.summary: A PNAS study led by Nova Southeastern University found fish, crustaceans and squid in the Gulf's twilight zone dropped about 60% from the year after the 2010 spill to 2015 and have not recovered since.

briefs.headline: ESA's Euclid telescope finds its first new comet
briefs.summary: Comet C/2026 S1 (Euclid) turned up in images taken Sept. 16 to 24 about 810 million miles from Earth, flagged by a University of Helsinki researcher's software. The Minor Planet Center confirmed it Oct. 8.

briefs.headline: NASA's simulated Mars crew marks a year inside habitat
briefs.summary: The four CHAPEA volunteers entered the 1,700-square-foot 3D-printed habitat at Johnson Space Center in Houston on Oct. 19, 2025, with communication delays of up to 45 minutes each way. They exit Oct. 31 after 378 days.

briefs.headline: DHS orders civilian agencies to drop DeepSeek products
briefs.summary: The Homeland Security order issued Monday covers DeepSeek products and third-party services developed with them. Luta Security's Katie Moussouris said the 'developed using' clause cannot be verified in practice.

briefs.headline: OpenCode breach runs up charges on users' AI accounts
briefs.summary: The open source coding agent said attackers broke into an older system Saturday, exposing API keys of 1.4% of OpenCode Console users. Developers reported charges in the hundreds of dollars; OpenAI said it is refunding them.

briefs.headline: Anthropic study ties drop in junior hiring to AI agents
briefs.summary: The company's own internal study says junior roles fell from 27% to 9% of technical new hires since early 2025 while its agents logged six times the hours of human staff by August. It says the results may not map onto the wider economy.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has Tuesday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster carries no regional line today; the Alberta result runs as the lead and not again in Canada.
